# LDBG

> LDBG is a free falling-block RPG you play in your browser. Every line you clear hits a monster. Gather on the Farm, craft gear, fight through Greenshore and duel other players.

LDBG is a falling-block puzzle game and an RPG at once. You stack falling pieces and clear lines as in any competitive stacker, and every line you clear does something in the RPG: on the Farm it gathers materials, in a dungeon it strikes the monster in front of you, and in the Arena it hits another player. Your account keeps your character's level, gear, materials and unlocks between runs. It is made with the Godot engine by an independent developer and is in early beta.

- Play free in a desktop browser: https://redredret.github.io/ldbg/
- Official site: https://redredret.github.io/
- Optional Windows app: https://github.com/redredret/redredret.github.io/releases/latest
- Controls: keyboard or controller, every action rebindable. Built for computers, not phones.
- Price: free. Guests can try a local demo; logging in keeps progress on the game's servers.

## The game in numbers

- 142 items, including 61 pieces of gear (helmets, armour, swords, bows, staves, bucklers, rings, necklaces), from 106 crafting recipes
- 16 kinds of monster, 8 of them bosses
- 19 fights in the Greenshore story route
- 107 upgrades across 3 upgrade trees (Combat, Skills and Build)
- 46 quests from 7 townsfolk, and 79 daily and weekly tasks
- Live totals, read 2026-10-21: 22 adventurers, 4,071 monsters slain, 1,377 bosses slain, 1,562 Quads and 893 T-spins cleared, 929 Farm runs

## The Farm

The Farm is an endless run. Clear lines to gather logs, ore, fish and fibre, then craft with them. Quads, T-spins and combos gather more.

- **Farm Solo**: Just you and the board. Garbage rises every few pieces, so keep clearing.
- **Farm Versus**: Up to ten players in a room, sending garbage at each other. You keep everything you gather.
- **Dark Farm**: Versus with stakes. Half of what you gather is on the line, and the winner takes it.

## Crafting and gear

Smelt your ore into ingots, weave your fibre into fabric, and work them into 61 pieces of gear across 106 recipes. Everything you wear shows on your character, from helmets and armour to swords, bows, staves, bucklers, rings and necklaces. Trade the rest for Gold with other players on the Market.

## Dungeons

Greenshore's story runs 19 fights long, from zombies on the shore to the Cult Leader at the top of the tower. Your lines are your attacks. Theirs land on your board: arrows knock out blocks, fire spreads along the bottom row, and slime costs you a rotation.

- **Story**: Greenshore's set route, through every area and every boss.
- **Endless**: Endless dungeon regions. The deeper you go, the better the rewards.
- **Dark Endless**: DANGER. A riskier, more rewarding endless dungeon. Fight other players for their gear, and higher monster drop rates, while risking your gear.
- **The Garbage Man**: 10 waves of garbage, faster every wave. One top-out ends it.
- **The Slime King**: A king after every king, alone or with a friend. He walls your board down to four columns until he falls.

## Bosses

- **Bandit King**: Switches between arrow rain and a blade spin that cuts your top and bottom rows.
- **Cyclops**: Knocks blocks loose from the top of your stack, then sets it on fire.
- **Punchy**: Slams the ground, and a stone wave sweeps across one of your rows.
- **Shooty**: Hurls boulders that drop three or four stone blocks onto your board.
- **Bernie**: A fire-casting cyclops whose fireball spreads along your bottom row.
- **Cult Leader**: Opens portals and hurls fireballs, then shields itself from your next hit.
- **The Garbage Man**: Throws garbage at you one line at a time, faster every wave. Beat wave ten for an Arcane Vault, then keep going.
- **The Slime King**: Walls your board down to four columns, slimes your tower and wraps you up until you shake him off. Beat him and a bigger one comes for you.

## Lesser foes

- **Zombie**: Swipes a block off your top.
- **Super Zombie**: Rakes off two or three.
- **Slime**: Slimes your piece. No rotating.
- **Squirrel**: Nips at you. Never your board.
- **Bandit**: Arrows knock out a block.
- **Bandit Elite**: A tougher bandit, crossbow and all.
- **Cultist**: Fireballs, and a stab at your bottom row.
- **Oak Entling**: A stump that refused to stay felled.

## The Arena

In the Hollow Spire you pick your opponent off the board. Look over their gear first, then fight for the win, or put a piece of your gear against a piece of theirs. Every hit you land is a line you cleared, so the better stacker usually walks away richer.

## Questions

### What is LDBG?

LDBG is a free falling-block RPG you play in your browser. Every line you clear is an attack on the monster in front of you. You gather materials on the Farm, craft gear, fight up the Greenshore dungeons, and duel other players, and your account keeps your levels, gear and loot.

### Is LDBG free to play?

Yes. LDBG is free and plays in your browser at redredret.github.io/ldbg. Try it as a guest, or Log In so everything you earn is kept.

### Do I need to download anything?

No. It runs in a desktop browser such as Chrome, Edge or Firefox. There is also an optional Windows app that opens the same game in its own window, with extra settings like higher frame rates; it isn't signed yet, so Windows asks you to confirm before it runs.

### What do I play it with?

A keyboard or a controller, on a computer. Every control can be rebound in Settings, and handling such as auto-repeat and soft drop speed can be tuned the way competitive stackers like it.

### Can I play on my phone?

Not yet. LDBG needs a keyboard or a controller, so play it on a computer. Touch controls are planned.

### How does the RPG side work?

Clearing lines gathers logs, ore, fish and fibre on the Farm, or deals damage in a dungeon. Bigger clears hit harder: Quads, T-spins and combos all pay extra. You earn XP and levels, spend points across 3 upgrade trees, craft and wear gear, finish quests and daily tasks, and open reward chests.

### Can I play with friends?

Yes. Farm Versus seats up to ten players who send garbage at each other, Dark Farm puts half your haul on the line, Endless and the Slime King can be fought with a friend, and the Arena lets you duel another player for the win or for each other's gear.

### Is my progress saved?

Yes. When you Log In, your progress is kept on the game's servers and follows you to any computer, and it stays through the beta: nothing you earn now will be wiped. Guest play is a short local demo, and nothing earned as a guest moves to an account.

### Is LDBG finished?

No, it is in early beta and grows every week. New dungeons, bosses, gear and modes land often; the Recently Added list on this page shows the latest.

## Recently added

- 2026-11-11, **Slimes share with the Little Slime King**: With the Little Slime King following you, ordinary slimes now drop everything five times as often: their Gold, Slime Balls, ores, logs and cloth, the Magic Ring, their rare finds and, in the Endless Dungeon, Slime Keys. In co-op it counts for the whole party. And the Slime King himself is harder to hold off: each hit now pushes his next attack back only 0.3 seconds instead of a whole second.
- 2026-11-11, **The Little Slime King loves slime**: The Little Slime King does more now. With him following you, every slime you fight takes 10% more damage, and Slime Kings drop Thick Slime and Royal Jelly five times as often: in his pit, as a golden king, and on the Endless Dungeon's roads. He still makes golden Slime Kings twice as likely, but he no longer leads you to the Slime Grotto. In co-op, his slime finds count for the whole party.
- 2026-11-10, **Gilded kits are a real prize now**: The Gilded Ornament Kit is much rarer, and it can come from anywhere. Every monster you kill has a one in a million chance to drop one, and a boss one in five hundred thousand. Every chest can hold one too, from one in a hundred thousand for a Wooden Chest up to one in twenty thousand for a Royal Chest. That covers region chests, Dark chests, the Garbage Man's vault, the Slime King's Royal Vault, and the chests from tasks, diaries and bounties. Every page of the Collection Log has a slot for one. Runs you started before this keep the old odds.
- 2026-11-10, **A new look for the menus**: The menus have a new look: buttons with a dark outline and a little grain, panels framed in wood, and flat, quiet backgrounds. Your fighter now stands beside the main menu, and the welcome screen lets you pick your hair as well as your skin tone. Nothing about how you play has changed.
- 2026-11-09, **Desert gear and upgrades**: The Red Desert's enemies drop new materials and gear now. Bring the right parts and you can upgrade older pieces at the crafting table: a Punchy's Hat, an Ipe Bow, a Cultist Book and more. An upgraded piece keeps its Forge roll and its ornament. The Cookhouse can make a Worm Steak too, if you can face it.
- 2026-11-09, **Wormlings**: Something small is waiting in the Dust Bowl just before the Desert Worm. The Wormling comes up out of the sand, bites one block at a time from anywhere in your tower, and heals for every block it swallows. Bring combos. It can drop a Worm Fang, and much more rarely a Magic Ring.
- 2026-11-09, **Wider drop tables**: Most enemies in the game drop more kinds of things now, from materials you can use to gear you can wear. Every enemy can also roll a Rare Drop: a separate table of bundles, Gold and rare parts for its home region, once a kill in every mode. Squirrels steal things, champions drop Scrap, and the Slime King finally pays a little Gold.
- 2026-11-09, **The Raider Scimitar**: The Red Desert's enemies have their own drop tables now, and the Scrap Warlord can drop tier four materials. Raiders and the Warlord can also drop the Raider Scimitar, a level 50 sword. One clear in ten sends a dust devil at the monster you're fighting for three extra hits, and against another player a big clear tears blocks off the sides of their tower. Mend one with Worm Fangs from the Desert Worm.
